items.locator: VA National Center for PTSD — PTSD and DSM-5, Criterion E: Alterations in arousal and reactivity; includes hypervigilance/being on guard, exaggerated startle response, concentration problems, and sleep disturbance. VA notes DSM-5-TR did not change adult PTSD diagnostic criteria.

items.locator: DailyMed Protamine Sulfate Injection, USP — Boxed Warning/Warnings and Dosage and Administration: rapid administration may cause severe hypotension and serious anaphylactoid/cardiopulmonary reactions; administer by very slow IV injection with dose based on heparin exposure/timing.

items.locator: DailyMed HUMULIN R (insulin human) — Dosage and Administration, routes of administration: administer subcutaneously; intravenous administration is permitted under medical supervision with close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium to avoid hypoglycemia and hypokalemia.
items.version: Eli Lilly HUMULIN R FDA label updated 2025-05-27; current DailyMed version live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A hospitalized client requires regular insulin, and the provider is considering intravenous administration. Which statement about HUMULIN R administration is correct?

options.A: HUMULIN R may be given subcutaneously; IV administration is permitted under medical supervision with close blood-glucose and potassium monitoring.
options.B: HUMULIN R is restricted to subcutaneous use, and intravenous administration is not included in the prescribing information.
options.C: Intravenous HUMULIN R can be given without extra monitoring because the route does not change hypoglycemia or potassium-related risk.
options.D: Intramuscular HUMULIN R is the preferred labeled route when a faster glucose-lowering response is required in the hospital.

items.rationale: The current HUMULIN R label includes subcutaneous use and allows intravenous administration under medical supervision with close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium because hypoglycemia and hypokalemia can occur. Option A states the labeled route and monitoring requirements. Option B incorrectly excludes the IV route. Option C removes required monitoring. Option D invents a preferred intramuscular route that is not the labeled hospital alternative described.

items.locator: DailyMed Potassium Chloride for Injection Concentrate, USP — Boxed Warning and Dosage and Administration: FOR IV INFUSION ONLY AFTER DILUTION; direct/undiluted administration may be instantaneously fatal and can cause fatal arrhythmia or cardiac arrest.
items.version: Hospira FDA label updated 2026-07-01; current DailyMed version published 2026-07-06 and live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.version: FDA digoxin tablets label updated 2026-01-29; current DailyMed label live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: DailyMed Ibuprofen Tablets — Warnings, Renal Effects/Advanced Renal Disease: long-term NSAID administration can cause renal injury; renal prostaglandin inhibition can reduce renal blood flow, with greatest risk in patients with impaired renal function; advanced renal disease requires avoidance or close renal monitoring when treatment is necessary.
items.version: Current FDA ibuprofen tablet labeling at cited DailyMed set ID; Renal Effects/Advanced Renal Disease sections live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease reports taking over-the-counter ibuprofen every day for musculoskeletal pain. Which teaching is most appropriate?

options.A: Regular NSAID use warrants clinician review because NSAIDs can reduce renal blood flow and worsen renal injury, especially when kidney function is impaired.
options.B: Daily ibuprofen is preferred in CKD because NSAIDs increase renal blood flow and protect remaining kidney function during long-term use.
options.C: Over-the-counter ibuprofen has minimal renal risk in CKD because nonprescription status indicates that daily long-term use is kidney-safe.
options.D: Higher ibuprofen doses are safer in CKD because stronger anti-inflammatory effects reduce the likelihood of NSAID-related renal injury.

items.rationale: FDA ibuprofen labeling warns that long-term NSAID use can cause renal injury and that prostaglandin inhibition can reduce renal blood flow, with greater risk in patients who already have impaired renal function. Option A therefore appropriately prompts review rather than assuming daily OTC use is safe. Options B and D reverse the renal-risk relationship. Option C incorrectly equates nonprescription availability with renal safety.

items.locator: DailyMed Haloperidol Tablets — Warnings, Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome: potentially fatal NMS includes hyperpyrexia, muscle rigidity, altered mental status, and autonomic instability; management includes immediate discontinuation of antipsychotic drugs plus intensive symptomatic treatment and medical monitoring.
items.version: FDA haloperidol tablets label updated 2025-01-28; current DailyMed label live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: DailyMed Alprazolam Tablets — Dosage and Administration §2.3 Discontinuation or Dosage Reduction; Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Dependence and Withdrawal Reactions: continued use can produce physical dependence; abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction may precipitate acute, potentially life-threatening withdrawal; use a gradual patient-specific taper.
items.version: FDA alprazolam tablets label updated 2026-02-19; current DailyMed label live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A client has taken alprazolam every day for several months and says, “I feel well, so I’m stopping it today.” Which teaching is most important?

options.A: Stopping today is appropriate because prescribed benzodiazepine use does not produce clinically important physical dependence.
options.B: Take a double dose every other day for one week and then stop because intermittent high doses prevent withdrawal more safely than a taper.
options.C: Do not stop abruptly; continued benzodiazepine use can cause physical dependence, and dose reduction should follow a gradual patient-specific taper.
options.D: Continue the current dose indefinitely because any attempt to taper a benzodiazepine is more dangerous than remaining on long-term therapy.

items.rationale: Current alprazolam labeling warns that continued benzodiazepine use can produce physical dependence and that abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction can precipitate acute, potentially life-threatening withdrawal. Option C accurately directs a gradual individualized taper. Option A denies dependence risk, Option B invents an unsafe regimen, and Option D incorrectly treats all tapering as contraindicated.

items.locator: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain — Recommendation 2 implementation considerations/adverse-effect counseling: constipation is common; when opioids are used regularly, prophylactic pharmacologic therapy such as a stimulant laxative with or without a stool softener is usually needed; stool softener or fiber alone should be avoided for opioid-induced constipation prevention.
items.version: CDC 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline remains current federal opioid-prescribing guidance; live MMWR source rechecked 2026-08-15.
